draft.title: Perimeter and area
card: Perimeter
the distance around the outside of a shape, in units such as cm. For a circle it is called the circumference: C = 2πr.
Area
the space inside a shape, in square units such as cm². Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × perpendicular height. Parallelogram: base × perpendicular height. Circle: πr².
Arcs and sectors
A sector is a slice of a circle, and its arc is the curved edge. Take the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle. Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr. Sector area = θ/360 × πr².
Composite shapes
Split the shape into simple parts, find each area, then add or subtract. Example: a 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle cut out has area 60 − 12 = 48 cm².
draft.remember: Perimeter is the distance around. Area is the space inside. Split composite shapes into simple parts.

a.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. What is its area?
a.why: Area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². 60 cm² is wrong because it leaves out the ½, which is the rectangle's area. 16 comes from adding the base and height.
a.clue: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

b.q: A sector has a radius of 6 cm and an angle of 90°. What is its area, to the nearest cm²?
b.why: The sector is 90/360 = 1/4 of a circle. Area = 1/4 × π × 6² = 9π, which is about 28 cm². 113 cm² is the whole circle. 57 cm² uses 1/2 instead of 1/4.
b.clue: Find the fraction of the circle first, then use πr².

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm², and ¼ × π × 6² = 9π ≈ 28 cm².

final.title: Perimeter and area
card: Perimeter
the distance around the outside of a shape, in units such as cm. For a circle it is called the circumference: \(C = 2\pi r\).
Area

the space inside a shape, in square units such as \(\text{cm}^{2}\). Rectangle: length \(\times\) width. Triangle: \(\frac{1}{2} \times\) base \(\times\) perpendicular height. Parallelogram: base \(\times\) perpendicular height. Circle: \(\pi r^{2}\).
Arcs and sectors

A sector is a slice of a circle, and its arc is the curved edge. Take the fraction \(\frac{\theta}{360}\) of the whole circle. Arc length \(= \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r\). Sector area \(= \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}\).
Composite shapes
Split the shape into simple parts, find each area, then add or subtract. Example: a 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle cut out has area \(60 - 12 = 48\text{ cm}^{2}\).
final.remember: Perimeter is the distance around. Area is the space inside. Split composite shapes into simple parts.

a.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. What is its area?
a.why: Area \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30\text{ cm}^{2}\). \(60\text{ cm}^{2}\) is wrong because it leaves out the \(\frac{1}{2}\), which is the rectangle's area. 16 comes from adding the base and height.
a.clue: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

b.q: A sector has a radius of 6 cm and an angle of 90°. What is its area, to the nearest \(\text{cm}^{2}\)?
b.why: The sector is \(\frac{90}{360} = \frac{1}{4}\) of a circle. Area \(= \frac{1}{4} \times \pi \times 6^{2} = 9\pi\), which is about \(28\text{ cm}^{2}\). \(113\text{ cm}^{2}\) is the whole circle. \(57\text{ cm}^{2}\) uses \(\frac{1}{2}\) instead of \(\frac{1}{4}\).
b.clue: Find the fraction of the circle first, then use \(\pi r^{2}\).
